narrative.overview: A registry treated as an exploded engineering plate rather than a gallery of cards. Every entry is a numbered part on a ruled sheet. A fixed index spine holds the totals; the center carries the parts list; an entry page carries the full sheet. The page behaves like a document you consult, not a feed you scroll. The atmosphere is cool, dry, and legible. Hairlines do the work that shadows would do elsewhere. Blue appears once, on the active selection and on actions, so it reads as a decision rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Two-column plate with a sticky index spine and a wide reading column
Numbered list rows with tabular mono indices instead of uniform cards
One accent, reserved for active state and controls
Status carried by a rotated square stamp plus text, never color alone

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is used only for active selection, links, and actions. If a region needs emphasis, use weight, scale, or a hairline instead.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Status is a rotated square mark plus its text name. The mark is filled only for available; shape and text carry the meaning without relying on hue.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every numeric value uses tabular figures so columns line up without alignment tricks.

dos: Do keep the index spine present from the first viewport on desktop and let the list use the full remaining width.
Do use tabular mono figures for every count and index.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion and remove the row entrance entirely.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color or a gradient.
Don't replace list rows with cards or add decorative icons.
Don't animate layout properties; use transform and opacity only.
